The 2**19 to 2**17 change gave a large gain, so more optimizer steps in 300 s may help further. Leave all LRs unchanged. Check that the LR/momentum schedules depend on elapsed time, not step count.

This cuts a large number of embedding parameters and the memory traffic of the embedding lookups and Adam updates, so it should raise steps/s. The test is whether the throughput gain outweighs the capacity loss at 300 s. Remove the dead code if it is simple to do so.

backlog.spec: Check how the loss is computed. If full float32 logits of shape (B*T, vocab) are materialised, compute the lm_head matmul and cross-entropy in chunks of 4096 tokens with torch.utils.checkpoint, so that the logits are not stored. This frees memory so that DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128 might fit, and is faster if memory bound. Keep the softcap and the loss identical. Report throughput.

Keep TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE in tokens and scale DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE up proportionally so that tokens per step stay the same. Attention cost drops and more steps per second are possible. Only do this if the evaluation call is not affected by the constant. If eval imports the sequence length from prepare, do not touch it; instead skip this idea and use a shorter window for the S layers (window = seq/8).

backlog.spec: Keep an EMA copy of the model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_) and swap the EMA weights in just before the final evaluation call. With roughly 131K tokens per step and many steps, an EMA often gives a gain in the low-LR phase. Because warmdown already goes to zero LR, use decay 0.995 to avoid lag. Do not alter the evaluation function itself, only the weights the model holds when it is called.
backlog.title: Weight EMA for evaluation

backlog.spec: Reduce the Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon from 5 to 3 (or 4 if that is the current value) to lower the optimizer cost per step. At 131K tokens per step the optimizer is a real fraction of step time, so more steps fit in 300 s. Keep the coefficients of the polar-express/NS iteration as they are for the first steps used.

backlog.spec: Add an auxiliary loss 1e-4 * mean(logsumexp(logits)^2) to the training loss only (not to the evaluation). It stabilises the logit scale and may allow a higher unembedding LR. Implement it in the training forward pass by computing the logits once and reusing them for both cross-entropy and the z-loss. Keep the evaluation path unchanged.
backlog.title: Z-loss regularization on logits

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown in the LR schedule function with a cosine shape over the same final WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.5 of the time budget: lr_mult = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*p)) where p goes from 0 to 1 across the warmdown. Constant LR before that. It is a one-function change and is a different decay shape from the linear variants already tried.

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 and ASPECT_RATIO = 96 (model_dim 576, 4.5 heads of 128 is not divisible, so also set HEAD_DIM = 96 -> 6 heads, or use ASPECT_RATIO = 85 rounded to 512 with 4 heads of 128; pick dim 512 and HEAD_DIM 128). This is a bolder reshaping, giving a wide-and-shallow model with fewer sequential kernels and higher throughput. Depth 6 at dim 384 was worse, so the width must grow to compensate; use dim 512, depth 6.

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE to 2**16 and DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE to 32 (or 64 if the sequence length makes tokens per micro-batch match), so grad accumulation stays at 1 micro-step per optimizer step if possible.
